fields.reasoning: The finding's two halves need different remedies, so I took both options it offered. Size: on a recount, the rest set's files outside the session-fixture and runtime groups hold far more tests than the session (214) or runtime (202) leaves, so splitting by prefix brings each half near their size. The session_/web_/inbox_/rex_ files share the daemon-and-pane state likeliest to need serial tests, so they stay together. Scope: a package-wide shuffle, race or timing failure can show up in any group's file, so whichever leaf owns those checks must be allowed to edit every internal/api _test.go file. Putting the checks on a separate last leaf keeps the other leaves' per-file scopes as they are. The intent's limits still hold on every leaf: test code only, no projection, no test skipped, deleted or merged.
fields.statement: api-tests-parallel-rest is split three ways. Two leaves parallelise its files, each touching only its own files: one takes the session_, web_, inbox_ and rex_ _test.go files that do not call newSessionFixture, plus plan_test.go and lifecycle_test.go (about 140 top-level tests). The other takes the remaining files outside the session and runtime sets: model_, change_, write_, read_, check_, lineage_, guide_, ci_ and the rest (about 195 tests). Each leaf's acceptance is shuffled-twice and -race over its own tests only, with a -run pattern built like the runtime leaf's. A third, finish leaf comes after all four parallelising leaves and may edit any internal/api _test.go file, never non-test code. It owns the package-wide checks: go test -shuffle=on over all of internal/api passes twice with different seeds, -race over the whole package reports no data race, go vet is clean, the test count from go test -list is unchanged, and the 150 s wall-time target holds. It fixes a cross-group race or shuffle failure by making that test serial with a comment, or by fixing its shared state.
